newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Positive outlook for wool in 1997 - WOOLTEL.
newsitem.headline: Positive outlook for wool in 1997 - WOOLTEL.

text.p: The outlook for wool textile production in 1997 continues to strengthen and the improvement should quickly be conveyed to raw wool markets due to generally low commercial stocks, wool newsletter WOOLTEL said.
One unfortunate outcome of low commercial stocks held globally, apart from in China where intermediate stocks were at high levels, was that raw wool markets were likely to be more volatile, it said.
"When downstream orders eventuate, decisions will have to be made quickly to locate sources for prompt delivery, hence the prospects of price volatility," it said.
But the supply situation in Australia would restrain the upward trend in average wool prices, it said.
Unsold stocks held by Australian brokers in late January were still 976,000 bales, slightly above January 1996 but well above the 567,000 bales in store at the end of January 1995, it said.
On-farm wool stocks also remained a burden, it said.
